Santaphobia

Horror

In 2019, the morbid, mangled bodies of filmmaker Emma Thomas (Lizzie Aaryn-Stanton) and her girlfriend Lauren White (Katie Martin) are discovered in the woods following a night at the notorious ‘Satan’s Grotto’ – a festive attraction that was home to a horrific holiday massacre in the early 1980s. A paranormal researcher (Emily Booth) presents the recovered recordings, narrating the footage as the two girls, and Emma’s father (Cory Peterson), embark on their perilous journey through the grisly grotto. At first all seems swell as they wander through the wicked winter wonderland, but when a mysterious figure appears on screen and her father disappears, Emma’s skepticism turns to obsession. Desperate to uncover the truth, Emma’s reality unravels as she discovers she’s trapped in an endless Christmas Day loop, where madness and violence are inescapable.

Ben'imana

DramaHistorieSci-Fi

Rwanda, 2012. The country is emerging from an era of silence after the 1994 Tutsi genocide, and people's courts are being set up with the aim of bringing justice and reconciliation. Veneranda, a survivor, is convinced of the need for these trials. Despite pressures, she organises discussion sessions between victims and the families of the executioners. Therapy for some, an act of betrayal for others, these testimonial sessions revive and reveal the traumas that each of them try to overcome, in their own way. The wounds of Veneranda's past are exposed again when she learns of her daughter's unexpected pregnancy and the identity of the father. Veneranda has to face her own contradictions and the dark parts of her past.
